pr_title: PromQL parser: support underscores in literal numbers
pr_body:
Support underscores in numbers, namely, decimals, hexadecimals, and exponentials.

Fixes #12769.
pr_comments: I will consult the team about this.

@roidelapluie Has there been any feedback for this yet? If not, lets kick off a thread in prometheus-developers / dev-summit?

_We looked at this in our bug scrub._

@beorn7 Sure, apologies for the delay here. I'll patch this up.
@rexagod do you think you can tackle the UI changes, too? We could also try to find a frontend expert to do it, but that's notoriously hard.

issue_context.title: Proposal: optionally support underscore in big numbers
issue_context.body:
### Proposal

Recently i found a merge request to internal monitoring with scientific notation in right side of expression. That is how currently users trying to cope with big numbers to make it "simple" to read.
Go and many languages now support input numbers with underscore in it.
Please make it possible in promql too. 

support information
https://go.dev/ref/spec#Letters_and_digits
https://peps.python.org/pep-0515/
https://www.javascripttutorial.net/es-next/javascript-numeric-separator/
comments: Where exactly would you like to support them?

in promql query language 
expression like 
`expr: metric_name > 10_000_000_000_000` 
simpler to read then
`expr: metric_name > 10e12`
This is quite a change, I will gather the team's opinion about it.

Did we ever collect the team's opinion about it?

I like it. It the same as in Go.

review_comments:
I'm thinking about some other edge cases we can add:
- `1_2_` as an invalid number
- `_1_2` as an accepted metric name/string. (to make sure this change doesn't break that)
- `1_e2` as an invalid number
Thanks
